title: Former NFL guard Jordan Devey, 38, died by suicide, family confirms
dek: Jordan Devey, a guard who won a Super Bowl with the New England Patriots in 2014, died by suicide on Tuesday at age 38. His family has stated they believed he suffered from CTE but cannot confirm it given the circumstances of his death. Devey appeared in 44 career games across seven seasons with five teams.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Jordan Devey, Super Bowl champion with the 2014 New England Patriots, died by suicide at age 38 on Tuesday.
bottom_line: Devey's death and his family's public account of suspected CTE underscore ongoing concerns about long-term neurological and mental health consequences for professional football players. What follows from this moment, including whether his family pursues a CTE diagnosis or contributes to research, will help shape understanding of how the sport addresses these risks.
body: Jordan Devey, a guard who won a Super Bowl with the New England Patriots in the 2014 season, died by suicide on Tuesday at age 38, according to a family statement.

Devey played seven regular-season games for the Patriots that championship year and appeared in 44 career games, including 21 starts, across seven seasons with five teams. His most significant role came in 2015, when he played 15 games with nine starts for the San Francisco 49ers, the year following the Super Bowl season. He retired in 2021 after playing one game for the Buffalo Bills in 2020.

In a statement posted to a fundraising page, the family said: "Tragically, Jordan took his own life, leaving his family to navigate an incredibly difficult and heartbreaking time." Devey's wife, Linsey, said in a social media post that he died days before the couple's 15th anniversary. He is survived by his parents, his wife, and their four children.

Devey's mother, Leslie, told Fox 13 in Salt Lake City that the family believed Devey suffered from chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, a degenerative brain condition associated with repeated head impacts. However, the family stated they will not be able to test for CTE given the way Devey died, leaving his suspected condition unconfirmed.

CTE can only be diagnosed posthumously through brain tissue examination. The family's belief that Devey suffered from the condition remains unverified, though their public statement raises continued questions about mental health and neurological health outcomes among professional football players.
Devey's death marks another loss from the Patriots' 2014 championship roster, a team that has faced increased scrutiny regarding player health outcomes in the years since that season.
